provenance.method: Provisional source-backed classifications, including mutually exclusive routes and conditional variants. All 250 chapter templates are retained in the event corpus. Counts describe curated authored records, not observed playthrough frequencies.

Connected effects recorded for mercy.
Events triggered by moveto shack.
Connected effects recorded for betrayal.
Connected effects recorded for return.
The survivor’s warning and Cylanna’s identification of the attackers.
If Malin raises an undead recruit, Drogan condemns his necromancy.
At time over the raiders return and the orcs retreat; alternatively the orc force may be defeated earlier.
After victory Drogan banishes Malin if he used necromancy; otherwise Malin chooses to leave to seek Volk despite his family’s opposition.
Volk proposes investigating the swamp and explains ghouls as transformed men.
Volk directs Malin to kill two ogres and teaches him to strip and animate their bones.
Another ogre’s looted bow can be used to make a skeleton archer.
After Malin chooses readiness for spirit training, his reflection challenges his conflicting ambitions and his trust in Volk.
Malin summons a ghost and regains control after it slips away.
Volk identifies the Whitefang clan as the orcs who killed Malin’s father; Malin admits vengeance is now part of the fight.
Weak ice can give way on a new turn, drowning a heavy living warrior or marring an undead unit in mud.
A surviving chieftain retreats, prompting Volk to order Malin to pursue him alone.
Volk asks Malin to meet him near Tath after the pursuit for a final favor, while he makes preparations.
Drogan refuses aid and Malin decides to remove him, while trying not to kill other townspeople.
The fleeing orcs arrive on turn five.
If the chieftain dies while Drogan remains alive, Drogan still refuses Malin entry.
Drogan’s death turns Dela against Malin and he decides to flee.
Malin can escape northwest after Drogan dies; defeating Dela without killing her or killing the orc leader after Drogan offers alternative victory.
Volk obscures guards’ vision but warns that close contact will reveal the party.
If the party takes too long, dawn and the alerted city guard prevent entry.
The gates are shut behind the intruders but will not hold long.
City guards enter and later more guards arrive as the search continues.
Karae recognizes Volk and opposes him.
After Karae falls, Volk senses an illusion break and identifies the vault in the northwest.
The intruders find the vault passage.
The guards keep pursuing and close the distance.
A unit finds the book; Volk demands it, but accepts waiting until escape.
Volk reveals a cellar tunnel leading out of the city.
If Volk reaches the tunnel first, he collapses it and leaves Malin to capture and execution.
If Malin reaches the tunnel first the party escapes.
Volk takes the book and dismisses Malin; Malin accuses him of using him and demands the book.
Sir Cadaeus arrives on turn six seeking vengeance for Tath.
Dela arrives on turn thirteen to kill Malin.
Volk curses Malin as he falls and drops the book.
A suitable unit retrieves the book and returns it to Malin’s camp.
If Volk, the paladin and Dela all die, Malin reflects that everyone is dead.
Dying Malin begins the book’s ritual and confronts the physical form and then the soul.
He conquers death but emerges cold and hungry for life energy.
He explores the caves, can solve local puzzles, and senses a powerful creature’s lair.
Entering Xanthric’s domain provokes the dragon to summon elementals.
Mal Keshar defeats the dragon, claims its lair, and declares himself Mal Keshar the Damned.
After sufficient repetitions an opposing unit may reach the book; Mal Keshar feigns pain and the hero takes it away.
In that book ending the hero leaves with it, the lair collapses and rumors later tell of darkness protecting patrols.
He finds Inky and catches her.
Many tentacled creatures appear and he flees.
Complete the potion puzzle: melt ice, fill a flask, and place it on the altar.
Complete the coffin puzzle: retrieve its key and bones, then cremate the bones.
A troll finds a mysterious egg and makes a decision.
The death of a great guardian sends woses into a frenzy and ends the trolls’ hopes.
When Ougl touches the amulet the golem crumbles, then reforms loyal to him.
Dacyn senses a great power and leaves; the undead receive reinforcements.
At time over the enemy has cut off retreat to Wesnoth; Dacyn returns and directs survivors to a trapdoor.
If contacted, cave dwarves offer help against trolls but refuse to evacuate; their tunnel offers an alternate passage.
Dacyn identifies the undead as the invasion’s rearguard and orders an escape by killing either sorcerer.
Killing Mal-Skraat opens the northwest route; killing Mal-Kallat sends the survivors east with her brother pursuing.
Controlling ten villages makes the mercenaries flee; alternatively Addogin’s defeat captures him and scatters his company.
After collecting herbs the player may decline payment, pay for the capital route, overpay to recruit Hahid, or defer the decision.
Opening prison cages frees knights who may join the party.
On turn eight Dacyn warns against detection; on turn ten or when certain enemy leaders die, Mal-Ravanal recognizes Dacyn and escalates.
Capturing villages reveals outlaws and eventually their hidden leader Shodrano.
Rilaka arrives with undead; the first of Rilaka or Shodrano defeated prompts Owaec to join, while the other threat remains.
Killing the jailer frees Dolburras; he reports an undead army near Knalga and offers to join.
The party discovers surviving defenders and debates saving them against proceeding north.
Mal-Ravanal confronts Dacyn on turn five and leaves the defenders a hostile parting gift.
Owaec can meet Yannic; if Yannic survives until departure his garrison can evacuate and send a later reward.
An ogre is captured when it starts its turn unable to move more than one hex; one reaching the edge escapes.
At time over at least 300 gold secures sufficient supplies; with less the player may continue in hardship or restart.
If Grug is present he can attempt to befriend wild ogres rather than treating all of them as enemies.
Dacyn opens the entrance, and he and Gweddry select up to six companions for the inner expedition.
The inner party opens the sanctum, defeats its guard, and is captured after retrieving the amulet.
Dra-Nak arrives on turn nine and demands soldiers; Owaec refuses and the orcs attack outside.
Owaec reaches the west end and may destroy the bridge; any units left east, including unrecalled troops, are lost.
The advance rider fails to intercept a scout, and the alerted necromancer orders prisoners brought forward.
The party frees prisoners brought forward by the necromancer, including the conditional rescue of Gaennell.
Dacyn loses control of the amulet; spirits appear, including Owaec’s father, and Owaec rides away.
Dacyn regains control on turn two; Owaec returns on turn three and vows vengeance.
The party gathers gold as dormant corpses and leaders awaken when encountered; surviving until time over or defeating the three named enemy leaders completes the scenario.
On turn six Mal-Ravanal imposes magical night and undead reinforcements arrive under fog.
On turn seventeen dawn pierces the fog; the undead begin falling back in later turns.
Mal-Ravanal reappears after his bodily defeat; Dacyn uses the amulet, refuses the darkness offering him undeath, and chooses to die.
After the required number of lich leaders die, the concealment spell breaks and Mal-Ravanal is revealed among the remaining liches.
Mal-Ravanal reappears after his bodily defeat; Dacyn uses the amulet, refuses the darkness offering him undeath, and chooses to die.
Enemies reduced to zero hit points are imprisoned for gold until the cells fill; losing the jailer ends this income.
The two alternative escapes after defeating one of the dark sorcerers.
Two alternatives for dealing with Addogin’s mercenary company.
Hahid’s payment menu offers return west, an assault route, overpayment, or deferred payment.
The surviving elves disperse and offer recruits according to the number killed.
At time over the main reinforcements arrive and the enemy withdraws; alternatively defeating all leaders ends the defense early.
The party reaches the prisoners and frees them to fight and escape.
A prisoner mage reaches an escape hex; alternatively clearing all enemy leaders can earn Seimus once rescue conditions are met.
Connected outcomes within the same encounter.
Muff Malal is defeated or escapes when the time runs out; Moremirmu’s survival changes the closing dialogue and possible companion.
Connected outcomes within the same encounter.
Connected outcomes within the same encounter.
When the master bowman is beaten, Konrad demands his weapon and oath; the castellan yields.
Burlin offers eggs and dwarves in exchange for killing the gryphon matriarch.
If Konrad agrees, he defeats the matriarch and Burlin shares eggs and crew.
If Konrad refuses, Burlin mobilizes his dwarves; defeating him stops his contract.
Konrad can free Ulfdain and his dwarves, who join against the queen.
If Dosh is present, he can negotiate with Stoneskins for a paid truce or fighters.

Defeating all enemy leaders gives victory and a tally of the plunder. At time expiry, withdrawal succeeds only if any Stoneskin pledge is affordable; otherwise the Stoneskins attack and the scenario immediately ends in defeat.
The gate is shut and the tomb’s magic gives Deoran clarity and rest.
Entering slave locations frees people; some reveal the central gate is collapsed and the eastern shaft is open.
Connected outcomes within the same encounter.
Connected outcomes within the same encounter.
Konrad finds a single trapped dwarf, then chooses whether to accept two kinds of dwarvish fighters or leave them for Knalga.
If Li’sar is defeated, Konrad captures her and Delfador obtains the Sceptre.
Connected outcomes within the same encounter.
Mirya triggers the volcano under Asheviere’s orders, forcing flight regardless of the chosen result.
Delfador urges the party onward as his speed spell fades and lava rises.
After the lich is defeated, Li’sar acknowledges signs of her mother’s crimes and joins Konrad.
When Urag is defeated he threatens to kill Mirya; Li’sar refuses to bargain and he kills her.
While concealed, the party can release penned animals and sabotage an armory.
The party finds wounded Warven and Li’sar secures his loyalty to the new alliance.
After the undead leader falls, the woses give Delfador powdered sapphire, enabling earth elementals.
Defeated leaders promise to join; Haldiel or Simyr may also persuade defeated mounted soldiers.

Optional cave-wall mining; some breached walls release floodwater.

Burlin’s optional proposal and the accept or refuse completion routes.
Excavation, capture, or escape alternatives during the Sceptre encounter.
Elven evacuation, losses, and recruitment after Konrad holds the crossing.
Staged rider relief followed by the final route-specific arrival or early victory.
Rescue the students, then escape with a mage or clear the royal forces to recruit Seimus.
Rescue Moremirmu; his later ally outcome depends on survival.
Li’sar’s conditional departure changes the opposing commander and completion route.
The optional Stoneskin bargain can determine whether a time-limit withdrawal succeeds.
Free slaves, escape with them, and receive supplies based on rescues.
Li’sar confronts Urag and Mirya’s ransom ends in her death.
Olurf’s passage decision and the mountain exit
The Ka’lian defense and news of the treasury
The assault on the treasury and the prisoners’ release
The gold recovery and escape
Kalenz hires Olurf to defend the flank
River monsters appear when the party enters the crossing.
Aquagar falls and curses Kalenz, Crelanu and all future owners of the book.
The elvish and human reinforcements
The infiltration, killing and escape
Landar’s coup and Kalenz’s escape
Kalenz’s final attempt to reach Landar
Landar is defeated and confesses that he secretly drank a second dose of potion.
Approaching the village awakens Remald and Wolmas, who join the defense.
A footpad can take a discarded pack and permanently increase ranged damage.
Tarwen demands the magistrate; Baldras refuses.
Tarwen’s death removes the remaining enemies; survivors report that some riders escaped.
Baldras can retrieve his good mace, gaining one melee damage.
Baldras acknowledges that they have made enemies of the Crown; peasant units transform into outlaws and recruitment changes.
Urk and Thhsthss dispute the promised payment.
A walking corpse appears when the northeastern water village is visited.
Tentacles emerge if a non-Baldras unit enters a particular water hex.
After the enemy leaders fall, the villagers find army-marked weapons and freshly minted gold; Baldras suspects the orcs were hired as scouts.
Maddock reports the king’s murder and the Queen’s conscription of village elders.
As Kestrel dies, he identifies his soldiers as Eldred’s magically accursed troops sent west by the Queen.
After defending the city Baldras requests help; Maddock directs him to a contact in Carcyn.
On turn four the attackers visibly decay; on turn seven their human appearance returns.
Link reveals the military presence and directs the party to his brother Hans and a southeastern forest path.
The party spots stationary guards and Baldras directs Harper’s faster people to scout.
If enemies can see a rebel at the start of their turn, nearby guards become aggressive pursuers; when no rebel is visible they return to idle.
Hans directs the party into the forest; Baldras must reach the exit.
Helicrom explains his mutual interest in weakening the throne and proposes attacks on patrols.
Additional royal patrols enter on scheduled turns, creating multiple successive interception opportunities.
A found key lets the player choose whether to open a coffin; opening releases a ghoul, whose death can yield a poison potion.
Helicrom reveals the flaws in the catacombs beneath the fortress and proposes removing the four supports.
Vashna’s offer of royal reinforcements is rejected by Dommel, and the orcs threaten the garrison.
Advance elements of Wesnoth’s main army arrive repeatedly, increasing pressure on the attackers.
Gwydion and knights of Elensefar arrive to fight Weldyn.
A unit entering each tower can demolish its support; after all four are destroyed, the stronghold begins to shake.
After all supports are destroyed, the fortress collapses during the later side turn, killing those inside; surviving leaders win.
Tallin frees Stalrag, negotiates with the lich brothers, and secures their aid.
Following the trail, Tallin emerges surrounded and learns the gold has gone ahead.
On turn 18 elvish troops may arrive with allied Eryssa, or hostile Eryssa’s promised gold may be delivered.
Rakshas receives his stolen gold and learns Tallin survived the trap.
The party finds Hidel dying; Eryssa grieves and takes command of the surviving elves.
If Sisal falls the orcs seize the gold and send it to the Master.
Turn-eighteen aid depends on whether Eryssa joined Tallin or remained hostile.
Tallin either enters the mines with Pruol alive or defeats Pruol before entering.
Tallin’s force is freed from the orcs, and the surviving orc Khrulg reports the uprising to the Master.
A royal crier calls landholding men to war; Rael departs with the village’s fighting men.
Maudie demands payment, brings naga ashore and orders the villagers enslaved; Elyn departs to warn the merfolk.
Diondra arrives with merfolk on turn 13, but says she has never met Elyn and is hunting the black ship.
Merfolk fighters and hunters become available to recruit.
Killing the wolf leader releases Red, a living man from its belly, who joins the party.
The first skiff is reached and repaired; the group still needs the other.
A second unit reaches the other skiff; both are secured and the group departs.
The party frees captive divers; Maudie then arrives with more captives, kills Elyn, and prompts the pursuit.
The naga retreat and Diondra and Thea order pursuit of Maudie’s ship.
Haldric and Rugnur agree on a sceptre and advance silver; Glildur contests the shipment.
Elven reinforcements arrive if the battle is still in progress.
A messenger goes to the city; retired warrior Baglur joins Rugnur and explains the gate mechanism.
Occupying all six glyphs closes the gate, leaving outside units cut off.
A dwarf reaching a cart discovers it can be ridden along the rails.
Disturbing the fungus-choked river floods the tunnel, while the rails remain usable.
The three principals reach the northern end and continue along the railway.
The talking gryphon Krawg offers help finding Thursagan while trolls and wolves close in.
Thursagan initially refuses and retreats; after repeated searches he agrees when he understands the challenge of containing the Ruby.
Thursagan reaches the cave exit and the expedition returns south.
Units find gold and coal; miners pick up the loads.
Delivery of one gold and two coal loads to the starting castle ends the mission; the resources may arrive in either order.
Durstorn refuses Glonoin’s price and orders the tools taken by force.
Krawg can summon another gryphon; the player gains Gryphon Rider recruitment.
Glildur arrives and offers Glonoin the spoils in exchange for the Ruby.
Glonoin’s defeat gives access to the workshops; the party must secure the caves or defeat enemy leaders.
Durstorn offers the Ruby in return for safe passage; the elves reject him and kill him.
Rugnur’s group plans the cave breakout and sends Alanin south with a request for help; Thursagan gives Alanin a rune.
Rugnur reaches the northeastern cave; if Alanin has already departed this ends the scenario.
Alanin reaches the southern border; if Rugnur has already entered the cave this ends the scenario.
Alanin identifies the faster riders behind him and seeks help from the local peasants.
Capturing a village can bring local villagers to Alanin’s aid.
Alanin reaches the fort and Hadlin admits him despite the pursuers.
The party encounters Khrakrahs, who claims the volcano as his lair and orders them out.
A unit discovers the enchanted, lava-heated forge.
After the extended turn limit expires with the forge defended, Thursagan emerges with the completed sceptre.
Glildur reaches the caverns with his pursuing elves.
An orc’s runic tablet is shattered in his fit and a troll’s tablet breaks when its bearer dies; either may occur first.
Breaking the final seal releases lava and gas; the dwarves die and the Sceptre remains buried unharmed.
Ardonna leaves before the Academy can apprehend her and considers obtaining bats from a ruined castle.
Encountering a wolf prompts a warning that fences can offer refuge.
Ardonna reaches the signpost and escapes; remaining outside at dawn is defeat.
Ardonna raises a human corpse and discovers that it is mindless.
A guard discovers the corpse and orders an attack for necromancy.
Capturing the guardhouse grants skeleton recruitment; losing it removes that ability.
Mossa spots the party; Ardonna suspects an ambush.
If Mossa dies, Garcyn vows vengeance.
Garcyn pleads for his life; Ardonna sees an opportunity for another experiment.
The captain learns a crew member has been killed and confines passengers while searching the ship.
Ardonna admits the stowaways are hers; negotiations fail and she summons them to fight.
When the captain dies Ardonna raises him, discovering he can still sail the ship.
The guards recognize necromancy; Ardonna decides all witnesses must die.
After the guards are eliminated a ghost appears, and Ardonna chooses to follow it.
Goblins identify Ardonna as a useful captive; she demands passage.
Exploration reveals the rear tunnel the ghost appears to have taken.
Ardonna enters the tunnel and follows the ghost onward.
Ras-Tabahn offers magical training to the young; Carcyn’s leader refuses.
Capturing every village or eliminating all defenders wins; jailed youths join and dark adept training is enabled for later.
Ras-Tabahn animates dead villagers and directs the adepts to practice attacks; initial recruiting is limited to turn one.
New corpse waves arrive on turns three and five.
After turn five the last enemy’s death wins and the saved gold is restored.
The saurians reject Ardonna’s plan to animate spirits; the nagas agree to assist them.
After the opposing leaders are defeated, Ardonna gains ghost recruitment.
Saurian Vendraxis asks to join in pursuit of a longer life; Ardonna accepts.
An elf confronts Ardonna over the disturbed dead; she asks to leave, but the forest awakens.
Woses appear repeatedly during the scenario.
Ardonna reaches the northeast corner and escapes.
Ras-Tabahn warns that gryphons inhabit the heights.
Exploring the bones can reveal a flightless bird and yield a skeletal rider; chocobone recruitment becomes available.
Both leaders reaching the northeast level ground ends the crossing.
Crelanu says he has given the book to elves to keep it from those seeking its dangerous secret.
Crelanu is defeated but restored to one hit point; he denies that magic prevents aging and says death is necessary.
Ardryn-Na believes his answer contains what they need, spares him and takes Ras-Tabahn to a cave.
The party finds giant spiders that may awaken.
The outpost ends when both leaders exit west or all spiders are eliminated.
The travelers discover mountain fire, which Ras-Tabahn says trolls use for crude armor.
The liches uncover the burial hall, where a guard seals the Troll Gate.
Ras-Tabahn finds a crack and clears a statue and coffin to make a route into the Crystal Caves.
If an approaching unit alerts the king, he obtains additional gold for soldiers.
Saurian reinforcements arrive on turn two; if Vendraxis is present, he refuses their demand to return.
Dwarven reinforcements arrive on turn three on easy or turn four otherwise; they have circled around the party.
A great mage arrives on turn twelve or when existing enemies are defeated sooner; only after this arrival does eliminating enemy leaders trigger victory.
An elvish leader arrives on turn thirteen if the battle continues that long.
After Alber falls a scout reports a much larger human army.
Kapou’e chooses between immediate withdrawal to seek the Council and staying to face the army.
On turn six Kapou’e recognizes the army’s strength and orders his people assembled while his fighters hold the humans.
When the people and treasury gold are ready, Kapou’e can withdraw via the signpost; if already there, departure triggers immediately.
Negotiations fail and Kapou’e decides to fight or pass the dwarves.
Blemaker and his son Grüü join the fight; the event also fires if the dwarf leader is defeated before turn four.
Kapou’e either reaches the mountain exit or defeats Kwili; after victory Grüü joins the journey.
A scout establishes that the elves mean to capture the shamans for humans.
Jetto can be freed from his cage during the battle; otherwise he asks for release after the elves are defeated.
The group stops to rest and discovers undead nearby.
Local orcs explain the attack and the evacuation to the Mourned Hills.
A sandstorm forces the party to seek the nearby oasis.
On sighting the oasis defenders, Kapou’e tries to explain the emergency but resolves to remove them.
Interrogation reveals a human agreement and the exiled prince’s territorial ambitions.
On encountering elves, Kapou’e orders a captive taken for questioning.
The party suspects elvish renegades in the unnaturally silent forest.
At the time limit, or when Shan Taum is defeated and surrenders, the Council interrupts the conflict.
The reunited Council asks Kapou’e to defend Prestim while it considers forming a Great Horde.
Inarix and her saurians arrive from the south with humans behind them.
The player may detonate after turn four once Kapou’e and Grüü are safe, even if Inarix is still stranded.
If saurian casualties are too heavy, future saurian recruitment is lost.
At the deadline, the Horde arrives: if any northern village is not controlled, rival warlords dispute leadership and the defense fails.
If all northern villages are held, the Horde joins the defenders and Lanbec’h retreats.
Merfolk join the attacking alliance and human transports support the assault; reinforcements arrive on scheduled turns.
Kapou’e challenges Lanbec’h, but learns that a subordinate commands the defense.
Kapou’e finds Borstep destroyed and pursues the attackers.
The dwarves hold the pass while the elves take their prisoners onward; humans remain to help.
Flanking forces arrive on turns four, five and seven, with Grüü arriving last.
When Thelarion is defeated he claims Shan Taum informed on Borstep and reveals the shamans were killed; their bodies are found in the lake.
In anger, Kapou’e orders the humans and elves in the area slaughtered.
Kapou’e accuses Shan Taum of spying for humans and causing the Council’s deaths.
Shan Taum sends Orga to fight and withdraws; the defenders are defeated.
Kapou’e finds Shan Taum has escaped.
At time over or if Lanbec’h is reduced to last breath, Howgarth intervenes and demands a parley.
Fresh human detachments arrive on turns six, ten and fourteen.
Howgarth denies knowledge of Karun’s assassination and identifies Shan Taum as the messenger who said Karun declined the Alliance invitation.
Shan Taum springs the ambush; Lanbec’h refuses Howgarth’s order to withdraw.
Shan Taum and Lanbec’h are killed; Kapou’e orders the traitor’s head displayed.
Howgarth escapes by gryphon to summon help and leaves bodyguards and gryphons to assist.
Lanbec’h is defeated before the turn-six withdrawal order.
Alternative actions in the mirror pool puzzle
Guide negotiations and the saurian matriarch encounters
Methor advances the apprentice to journeyman and names him Delfador; Garard gives him a special assignment.
Elende confronts the travelers with reflected selves and glimpses of their fears and futures.
An orc shaman’s defeat can give Delfador equipment from which he expects to imitate her draining attack in the next battle.
Orc encirclement, Asheviere’s capture and Lionel’s relief
Guide negotiations and the saurian matriarch encounters
Undead emerge while the companions guard the central cave; hostile entrances can be collapsed.
Delfador frees the spirit Aethyr, who says Iliah-Malal deceived and bound him.
Ghuvog yields; Garard claims the territory and spares him on condition that the orc clans withdraw.
Mortally wounded, Arand denies treason, says Eldred and Asheviere are the conspirators, and explains he mistook the attackers for the queen’s agents.
Garard’s murder, Deoran’s evacuation and Eldred’s betrayal
Delfador and Eldred’s final confrontation
After Bashnark falls, his dwarvish loremaster cloak-pin is discovered.
Approaching a grounded gryphon awakens it; an attack leaving a gryphon alive below 10 hit points captures it.
At time over, or when a capture leaves no hostile gryphons, Ratheln asks for aid; captured gryphons become the player’s riders.
Perrin asks Ratheln to accompany the dwarves as the other mages return to Alduin.
Masked dwarves demand the refugee; Angarthing invokes the Law and banishes their spokesman, and their side becomes hostile.
A stairway behind the throne reveals Karrag fled below; the party follows to prevent his spell.
Exploration encounters locked gates, masked guards and transport runes; activation enables movement between runes and the central gate.
After Dufon falls, Angarthing reaches the marked hex and opens the gate; Karrag can recruit undead and the objective changes to defeating him.

Defeat or survive until time out, with Moremirmu joining only if rescued and alive.
Defeat Li’sar before she leaves, or defeat Yrogin after command changes.
Affordable withdrawal, early victory, and unaffordable pledge failure are distinct outcomes.
Isolde withdraws after defeat or at the time limit.
Khargol’s death releases Fagh-Mok and triggers the succession fight.
Bashnark’s death leads to discovery and recovery of his cloak-pin.
Glashal’s defeat leads to battlefield discovery and the mages’ departure.
Dufon’s death reveals the sealed gate and Angarthing’s next location.
Karrag’s death ends his rule and the surviving dwarves plan restoration.
The refugee’s account triggers conflict with the masked dwarves and rescue of the villagers.

Orc arrival and Addroran’s defense order.
Haldric’s request for supplies and the drakes’ attack.
The sewer wizards and the sewer exit form the optional early-finish encounter.
Shek’kahan’s defeat and the optional remaining-leaders encounter.
When Fastik is beaten he tries to flee; Gerrick intercepts him and Hylas keeps him alive for questioning.
Ethiliel’s rescue and Nalmath’s attack
Deoran’s allegiance choice and its branch outcomes
Deoran and his companion reach Southport and learn that he must return to Westin immediately.
The rear guard, turn rewards and alternate victory
The lich withdraws deeper as Deoran pursues, explaining his hatred and ambition.
At the final confrontation Mebrin brings down the cave and dies, trapping Deoran’s force.
On the Afalas route, he and Galdrad arrive with Mebrin’s skull; Ethiliel accepts the evidence and ends the attack.
On the underground route, Deoran emerges with the skull after digging out with trolls; Ethiliel accepts the truth and stops the attack.
Westin’s siege, reinforcements and Mebrin’s defeat
Mordak falls; scouts report that Baran has been captured and taken north.
The elves refuse passage, believing the prisoner is a necromancer.
On sighting the kidnappers, Muff Toras drops his disguise and summons undead; the elvish side becomes allied to Arvith.
Muff Toras is captured at last breath, gives the castle location and two randomly selected passwords, and is bound for the journey.
On easy difficulty Brena offers to join; Arvith can accept her or instead take 70 gold.
At the first challenge Arvith chooses a password; a correct one lets the guards leave and he releases the captive adept.
A second guard wave arrives on turn three or six depending on whether first guards remain; if challenged, a correct second password dismisses that wave.
Rotharik’s death yields the cell key.
The party can discover Baran’s cell before or after obtaining the key.
Once Rotharik is dead, Arvith reaches the cell and frees Baran.

The player chooses to aid the dwarves or the trolls; the other side becomes hostile.
The chosen ally’s leader withdraws for reinforcements, and additional allied forces can arrive later.
A cloaked figure is driven off; this and victory over the opposing leaders are both required before proceeding.
The allies reveal a secret passage to the enemy chief’s stronghold and request an attack.
Grimnir waits until the elves are positioned, then blows the wall and leaves to report to his king.
A troll interrogator threatens a dwarf prisoner; Rogrimir can be saved and pledges to guard the elves.
Trolls destroy a bridge, while lava, heat and fire guardians threaten the passage.
The troll chieftain is killed; Grimnir says the trolls are retreating and offers shelter for the refugees.
Zurg waits for the elves to position themselves, breaks the wall and returns to report.
Grog can be rescued from dwarves and pledges a life debt.
Dwarven scouts’ charges fail; Jorgi orders backup charges after he is beaten or the attackers cross.
The dwarf chieftain falls, and Zurg offers caves and an escort for the refugees.
Underground enemies dam the river, sending floodwater into the caves and forcing a rapid escape.
The party may encounter an ancient training hall and fight apparitions of its former inhabitants.
At an outpost Kaleh questions the wounded cloaked figure, who describes the desecration of their dead and the name Yechnagoth.
The party reaches the surface; the guide remains loyal because the route back is flooded.
An apparition claiming to be Eloh orders Kaleh to submit to Durstrag; Kaleh refuses and the humans attack.
Nym warns that Durstrag has ordered riders to summon reinforcements; the party must stop them.
After Durstrag’s defeat Nym returns with merfolk emissary Esanoo, whose companions are captive; the elves agree to help.
At turn 16, captives still held are sacrificed; too few survivors means failure.
After all are freed or sufficient captives survive to the deadline, the human leaders withdraw and Tanstafaal presents a false Eloh who condemns Kaleh.
Zhul pleads against the fighting; the apparition immobilizes her if this scheduled scene occurs before it is defeated.
Kaleh defeats the apparition and Tanstafaal; Tanstafaal kills himself and Kaleh offers the rebels amnesty.
The merfolk offer to pilot four human vessels; capturing them permits the refugees to leave.
Once Kaleh captures a keep, merfolk bring in the other ships and offer reinforcements.
The party discovers the citadel’s hidden door and two keyholes.
The saurian and undead leaders each carry one of the two keys; discovery can occur before or after the door.
After the keys and entrance are found, false Eloh reveals the keys were a test and invites Kaleh inside; Nym and Zhul follow despite his request to go alone.
Defeating the false Eloh breaks her spell and reveals Yechnagoth’s monstrous form.
Destroying all three pulsing spires weakens the central body.
The weakened central body is defeated and Yechnagoth dies.

events.description: Dacyn reveals that Mal-Ravanal is his former friend Ravan and recounts their previous confrontation.

evidence.quote: name=victory_cutscene
[message]
message= _ "I suppose you have a right to know of the adversary we face. Mal-Ravanal was, at first, a mage of the realm like me. His fall began during the reign of our previous king, Haldric VII..."

message= _ "The King endeavoured to seek this peerless savant. In all the land, there were two magi that clearly stood out from the rest. Myself, and my good friend Ravan, a mage from the east. The King, wishing to choose the best advisor, sent us both before Eryssa. Then he conversed with the seer privately. None know what was said, but when he came out he announced that the seer was dead, and she had... chosen... me as the King’s new advisor."

message= _ "Before the incantation could finish, I summoned the utmost of my power and rended Ravan’s physical body. Yet even as I witnessed flesh and blood burn away into soot, a dark shadow arose from the ashen bones and dispersed throughout the sanctum. I knew then that death would be but a mere inconvenience to one so skilled in the mystic arts, and that Ravan’s spirit would return one day..."

events.description: Gweddry chooses to cross east behind enemy lines or west through Soradoc on the northern expedition.
conditions: The outlaws and undead are defeated.

evidence.quote: message= _ "Yes. But hope is not yet lost. After pondering the matter once more, I have come to a conclusion. I do not have the power to defeat Mal-Ravanal as I am now. We must travel north, away from Wesnoth, back to the sanctuary where I had defeated Ravan once before."

message= _ "If we fail to defeat Mal-Ravanal, no effort of ours will be sufficient to withstand the endless armies of the dead. Our blood is limited and the more it is spilled, the more their strength grows. Only by using the power from the sanctuary to destroy the Lich can we find salvation."
label= _ "Cross the Great River to the east, behind enemy lines. (normal)"
next_scenario=06a_Undead_Crossing
label= _ "Cross the Great River west in Wesnoth, near Soradoc. (challenging)"
next_scenario=06b_Soradoc

evidence.quote: message=_"True, true, but, well, you know, I suppose there’d really be no harm in coming with you even if you don’t get them all— yes, I think I’ll join you no matter what. You seem the nice sort, very chivalrous and all that."

message=_"But— err, of course I suppose I wouldn’t really be of much use to you unless you can gather at least some ingredients so that I can get my — you know — alchemical concoctions prepared. The more the better!"
message=_"And with that— yes, with that, I have everything I needed from the north! Excellent! I wonder what substances I should turn my study to next..."

message=_"Hmm? Oh yes, yes, that’s quite right, of course. In fact I’ve got some new ideas that I’m just longing to pursue; perhaps joining you on your travels will provide me with a good opportunity for travel and research. I’d be glad to accompany you on your travels, Konrad!"
message=_"Jeniver has said she will still follow us even if we run out of time, but without all three ingredients she also won’t be as useful as she might otherwise have been."

message=_"Oh, yes, no I understand; that’s quite all right. If you’ll have me, of course!"

events.description: An elven unit dies instead of escaping during the evacuation.
conditions: Elves escape or die while Konrad’s force holds the crossing.

evidence.quote: description=_"Survive until all elves escape or die ($dead_elves dead so far)"
message=_"The elves are going south across the river, but we must stand our ground and help them escape!"
name=die
speaker=Konrad {KONRAD_VARIATION glad}

events.description: Muff Malal is defeated before time expires.
conditions: Muff Malal is defeated before the time limit.

evidence.quote: message=_"Ugh, forget this! I’m not wasting any more time here with you — time for my dashing escape!"
message=_"The necromancer is defeated, and the countryside is safe once more! Good work, everybody."
message=_"The Light shall always find the Light, and so have I found you! Let us quest on together in opposition to the dark queen!"
message=_"The necromancer is defeated, and the countryside is safe once more! I am sorry that Moremirmu has perished, but at least he did not die in vain. Now we must continue onwards!"
result=victory

events.description: Chief Khargol dies, allowing Fagh-Mok to claim command and triggering the succession fight.
conditions: Khargol is defeated.

evidence.quote: message=_"Now is my chance! Set me free, girl, so I can take command of the horde!"
message=_"Go. But don’t you dare betray us, or I swear to personally find you and kill you. If you know anything about me, you’ll know that’s a promise I can keep."
message=_"As head of Khargol’s personal guard, is only right that I assume the late chief’s duties! Long live chief Fagh-mok the Amazing!"
message=_"Fagh-mok? You?! You’re weak! You were nothing more than the chief’s sword-carrier!"
message=_"I say we kill all three of ’em! Warriors, fight to make me chief and I promise to bathe you all in gold and blood!"

message=_"Not exactly, no. But at least he held up his end of the bargain, and we ours. Chief Khargol is dead, and until the Whitefangs resolve their succession crisis they’ll be of no aid to Asheviere."

events.description: Konrad’s party defeats the Great Icemonax, and Jeniver extracts its bile.
conditions: Great Icemonax is defeated.

evidence.quote: message=_"Oh, ah, I neglected to mention: only the Great Icemonax have the requisite liver chemistry for producing bile. You’ll have to down one of the bigger ones before I can collect what I need."
message=_"Oh, the Icemonax is dead! Yes, yes... allow me to extract the bile..."
message=_"Smoke! Yes, earth turned to air... most useful for befuddling and bewitching the unprepared, and a validation of my theory of elemental humors!"
message=_"You have the spider venom! Fantastic! I shall just add a distillation of euphoria... a dash of elf-hair, a few other bits and bobs..."

message=_"Ugh... well, so much for my treatise on the life-extending properties of venoms. Ah, well— well, setbacks are inevitable! At least the toxin, properly prepared, may make for a useful weapon."
message=_"Fantastic, the Yeti is defeated! Let me take a look at that tongue..."

message=_"Err, well, no, not quite. It’s more of a... distillation — yes, a process for refining and extracting more value out of your existing coin. But “transmutation” is a much more exciting word for alchemists. And etymology aside, my discovery will certainly help boost your income!"

events.description: Delfador confronts the apparent drake; defeating it reveals Iliah-Malal’s illusion and his role in directing the saurian alliance.

evidence.quote: message=_"You! With so many undead about I was expecting to find the necromancer... I don’t entirely understand what’s going on here, but I do know that you’re an enemy of Wesnoth, and that’s good enough for me."
message=_"YOU INVADE MY HOME.
message=_"Well fought, Delfador! They warned me you were dangerous, but to have found me amidst all the vastness of the north — you have truly exceeded all expectations!"
message=_"Now the story begins to make sense. The Omaranth I saw was never more than an illusion. You are Iliah-Malal."

message=_"You wiped out this flight of drakes, and took the visage of their leader. You led the saurians to join Clan Blackcrest, and you sent them to war against Wesnoth. But why? How does all this fighting benefit a mage?"

events.description: Iliah-Malal offers Delfador power if he abandons Garard; Delfador refuses.

evidence.quote: message=_"How does all your fighting benefit you? Decades of war, and what has been gained? While you bleed for a failing country and an aging king, your whole life is passing you by. You’re on the wrong side of history, Delfador war-mage."

message=_"But you don’t have to be. Walk away! Stop wasting your life in service of an old man, and finally act for yourself! Delfador, I have allies under whose patronage you could live like a king, if you would only accept them!"
message=_"Like a king? I already serve a king, Iliah-Malal, and am well-loved for it. Protecting Wesnoth is my duty. King Garard is my friend. I hope you did not think to break me down so easily."
message=_"Bah, remain a fool, then. You will not find me so easily broken either."

events.description: Delfador releases the freed spirits to pass on rather than fight the living.

evidence.quote: message=_"I should... have kept... my potion..."
message=_"Elende’s prophecy rings true once more: “A figure of shadow cloaked in the spirits of the dead”... Good riddance. His meddling in life and death has been the cause of great evil."

message=_"I am free... free! You have breathed into me a ravenousness for life anew, life to drain from those who roam unfettered under the pale sun. Take us into your service, Delfador; lead us to your foes! Lead us against the living!"
message=_"No, no! Do not tempt me, I beg you, for that way madness lies... should I ever start down that dark path I would never become free of it."
message=_"No. But you have been of great service today, and for that you shall be rewarded with peace."
message=_"Return to your land of calm and quiet, and trouble the living no longer. I shall save my country without your help."

message= _ "Shut it, all of you! I don’t know why any of youse care what some off-brand dragon says, but don’t forget that you lizards made a deal to fight with us against Wesnoth. Even paid us for the privilege, you dumb little worms!

message= _ "Oh yeah? Try me, you filthy sacks of lizard slime; I’ll teach youse your proper place! To arms, Blackcrests!!"

evidence.quote: message=_"After all this time... Wesnoth is finally at peace. It is as if a veil of shadows has been lifted from upon my eyes!"
message=_"Delfador, you rascal, you’ve truly outdone yourself this time. They tell me how you turned the saurians against the orcs, sowed chaos from behind; truly incredible!"

message=_"“The Great” you were called by the enemy, and “The Great” you shall be called until the end of your days. Kneel, Delfador, war-mage of Wesnoth. And rise, “Delfador the Great”, High Advisor to the Crown!"
message=_"Now come, let us celebrate my— our— ...all right, your success! Victory! Victory! Victory by the name of Delfador!!"

evidence.quote: message= _ "I— yes, you’re right! With Garard dead, Delfador commands the greatest honest force left in Wesnoth, and he has no idea what has just transpired! Delfador must be warned."

message= _ "If we are lucky, we may yet be able to save Arand from Delfador’s ill-informed assault. But even barring that, Delfador’s leadership can surely rally enough soldiers to oppose Eldred by force of arms!

message= _ "Nothing so heroic. Wesnoth’s forces may believe me a conspirator now, but I will not give up on them so easily. If I fight my way into a private audience with each leader I’m sure I can make them see the truth about Eldred — Garard’s poor family relationships were no secret.

message= _ "When at last my strength is spent, I will flee through the forest — my steed is elf-stock, and no rival bred in Wesnoth can outpace its haste amongst the trees. But the more support I can garner now, the better our position will be in the future!"
message= _ "Now make haste, and godspeed! You must reunite with Delfador; I will send what soldiers I can spare after you!"

events.description: Delfador rejects Eldred’s offer to restore his title and chooses to oppose him.

evidence.quote: message= _ "We don’t have to fight the entire army or deal with Weldyn. The capital is too well-defended for us to sack outright — Eldred is the objective here."

message= _ "Once the truth gets out about Garard’s death, we’ll have enough allies to liberate Weldyn and more besides. But only if we can stop Eldred here and now — can prove to the watchers that this coup is not yet over; that justice and honor and hope still live in Wesnoth! That’s our goal today."
message= _ "Delfador, welcome! I was wondering if we’d get an appearance from you old has-been! ’fraid you’re not as popular with Mother and me as you were with old Garard."
message= _ "Just lay down your staff and greet me with open arms. You can even have your old title back! “Delfador the Great”, High Advisor to the Crown — don’t you agree that has a nice ring to it?"
message= _ "I am no longer so foolish as to be tempted by that, young prince! Enough blood has been spilled on your behalf; stop this madness and give up the throne, or I shall make you."
message= _ "Oh no, I don’t think so. You forget you’re speaking to your king, old man. Soldiers, attack! ATTACK!"

events.description: Eldred admits he feared Garard and moved against him first.
conditions: Battle continues to the corresponding turns

evidence.quote: message= _ "A future for me? I can count on one hand the times the old tyrant had anything kind to say about me."
message= _ "I wasn’t going to wait around to be disinherited, or worse. It was always going to be him or me — I just beat him to the finish."
message= _ "And don’t think that I have any illusions about what sort of snake Mother is either. I know, believe me. But she’s the snake who’s made me king, and that’s good enough."

message= _ "This wasn’t the first time Mother’s gone after Garard, you know. In the early days of the war, she betrayed his plans to the Whitefangs; fled to the orcs while they surrounded you and him both."
message= _ "You and Deoran brought her back, of course, and Lionel fought Garard free of the orcs. My childhood would have been so different if things had succeeded..."

evidence.quote: message= _ "We’ve explored the village, and I think we’ve rescued the last of the survivors."

message= _ "Last night, before the rock storm, I heard a voice in my sleep. It sounded like sweet music, and somehow I knew it was Eloh. I still remember her exact words: “You must be strong, young elf, for you enter a time of peril. The home you know will be destroyed, and you must lead your people to a new land. To the north you will find salvation and peace. Cross the desert and head to the mountains. Fear not, for I will guide you and protect you.” I’m not sure why I’m the one she chose to appeal to, but if this is her will, I will see it done. Our home is gone and the desert is a harsh place. If Eloh has prepared a new home for us, then I will lead us there."
message= _ "Then let us collect what supplies we can from the wreckage and head north with great haste. Our home is protection no longer, we must find a new haven for our people."
message= _ "I agree, we should not forget our dead. We should build a huge pyre and burn them with proper ceremony, so that the smoke may carry them on to the next realm."

message= _ "And so it was done. The dead were laid reverently on top of what little wood we could find. But the fire was big enough to burn the bodies to ashes and speed their souls to the hereafter. I remember at the time that the death of so many of our people was not the best omen for the start of such a large journey. They were the first of our people to die in this great endeavor, but they were to be far from the last."

events.description: The dwarves withdraw after their chieftain falls.

evidence.quote: message= _ "Faugh! Even in death I curse you! You will never escape these tunnels alive!"

message= _ "Little elves fight good. Zurg impressed. With dwarf chieftain dead, cowardly dwarves flee before us. Our struggle not over, still much more fighting, but elf and troll have won this battle. We thank you. Great Leader has allowed you to come speak with him. Great honor, never has one of your kind been allowed in his presence. But he wishes to talk with you and reward you. Please come with me."

message= _ "Shh, you two. Yes, of course, we would be honored to come and meet the Great Leader. But first, we left many of our people back up near the entrance to the great cave where you first met us and I fear that even now those caves aren’t safe. Can you help us escort my people to safety?"

message= _ "Hmm, yes, yes we can help. We have a few big caves you little people can stay in, and I get some big trolls to help escort you there. The Great Leader wouldn’t want any unpleasant surprises. Show me where your people are hiding and we will help you move them to our caves."

events.description: Underground enemies dam the river, sending floodwater into the caves and forcing a rapid escape.

evidence.quote: message= _ "Foul elves, you not escaped us yet. Great Leader will be avenged! We plugged river and you all drown with us!"
message= _ "Foul elves, you have not escaped yet. Our chieftain shall be avenged! We have dammed the river and soon all shall drown in its dark waters. Come join us in death!"
message= _ "That sound must be the rushing water. We have to get our people out of here, and fast!"
message= _ "No, but the water is rising to the southeast as well. The river must lead to more tunnels than we first thought."

events.description: The party may encounter an ancient training hall and fight apparitions of its former inhabitants.

evidence.quote: message= _ "This looks like a training hall. There are still a few old swords and spears lying in the corners. But otherwise it seems quite abandoned."
message= _ "All right you runts, let’s try this again. Pior, remember to swing your sword with your whole body, not just your arms."
message= _ "Wait a minute, I don’t see any targets or practice dummies. Who are they supposed to be attacking?"
message= _ "I believe that would be us. But perhaps we can give them a few lessons in proper fighting style."
message= _ "Sniff, who were those children? Why did they die, in the dark, so many years ago? May Eloh shine her eternal light upon their souls."

events.description: At an outpost Kaleh questions the wounded cloaked figure, who describes the desecration of their dead and the name Yechnagoth.

evidence.quote: message= _ "Fool. That did not stop their dark power. Nothing could stop them. I felt the rush of flying spirits, and the unbearable cold, so cold. For a moment I felt their torment. But no, they wouldn’t kill me. They let me go as a witness and laughed as I scrambled over the dunes."

message= _ "I was able to follow your trail, and I slipped among your people. No one noticed me, no I was too sneaky. And you wondered how I managed to follow you through the tunnels? Hah, you escorted me."

message= _ "You abandoned them! The pain, the agony, I still see their ghostly faces and hear their wails. And the necromancers kept chanting one name over and over: Yechnagoth, Yechnagoth, it reverberated in my ears. And every time I sleep I hear that name, and laughter, hideous laughter. She kept telling me it was your fault. And I believed her. Kaleh, forgive me, I just wanted to make the pain stop."
message= _ "He’s dead. Rest in peace. Oh, what have I done? All our dead kin, desecrated and tormented for eternity."

events.description: Kaleh’s party reaches the surface and leaves the flooded caves.

evidence.quote: message= _ "Look, the tunnel slopes sharply downwards to the left. And it’s big enough that it should divert most of the rising water."

message= _ "Grog, thank you so much for leading us out of the caves. We never would have found our way without your help. But with the tunnels flooded, how are you going to find your way back to your people?"

message= _ "Truth is that Grog not know much of sunlight lands. Sun and stars are scary, everything is open, exposed, no safe places to hide. But Grog cannot go back through all that water. And Grog doesn’t know where to find other tunnels back to his home. He is as lost as elves are."

message= _ "But Grog not afraid. Great leader told Grog to guide and protect elves, and Grog will keep his oath. Grog will follow elves wherever they may go and protect them from danger as best he can. Maybe later, Grog will find another way back down to the caves of his people. But for now, Grog will continue to serve and protect you."

message= _ "But my king told me to protect you from all dangers, and I plan to keep that oath. I do not like the above ground, it is too open and exposed; I feel that I could be attacked from any direction. But an oath is an oath and so I will follow you and your people wherever you may go and protect you as best I can. The tunnels cannot stay flooded forever; later perhaps if am able to return this way, I may be able to find my way back to my homeland. But for now I am yours to command."
message= _ "Praise Eloh, it is so good to be outside again. To see the sky stretching out above me, to feel the wind in my face..."

uncertainties: Source record includes multiple effects; this entry classifies one effect.

events.description: An apparition claiming to be Eloh orders Kaleh to submit to Durstrag; Kaleh refuses and the humans attack.

evidence.quote: message= _ "Now, in the valley live a group of humans who have also seen the light. They may seem strange, but they are my obedient followers. You must trust them, they will show you the way north. Follow them and they will lead you to me."

message= _ "I have no idea what you’re babbling about, elf, but you’re just lucky you caught me on a good day. You get to explain everything to the Iron Council. Now you and your people just lay down your weapons and we will take you into custody to be judged. They’ll deal with you as they see fit."

message= _ "Kaleh, I am Eloh, bearer of the staff of Ishtar and slayer of the demon-god Zhangor. Submit to him or I shall abandon your people to suffering and death. Your bones will litter the sand dunes, and vultures shall pick at your flesh. I am a just god, Kaleh, but no more forgiving than the harsh desert sun."
message= _ "Then kill me if you must, but I will not give myself over to those who threaten me and my people. I have not come through peril and darkness just to surrender to one such as you."

message= _ "You dare defy me?! All who refuse to submit to the authority of the Iron Council shall be killed. By the Dark Lady, I shall not put up with this bickering any longer. To battle, men! Drive those heathens back into the caves!"

message= _ "You are not the god I grew up with. You may be all-powerful, but I will not be your puppet. I am still their leader and as long as I draw breath I will do what I think is best for my people."

events.description: Nym warns that Durstrag has ordered riders to summon reinforcements.

evidence.quote: message= _ "Anyway you’ve really gotten us into a mess. The good news is that the outpost isn’t guarded as heavily as you might think. The garrison seems only half-manned. They obviously didn’t expect any serious attack to come from this direction."

message= _ "The bad news is that I overheard the commander ordering a special group of his men to get ready to ride north and summon reinforcements. It seems that the humans have a bigger village to the north. This outpost is lightly guarded enough that we might be able to defeat them, but in our weakened state if they bring the full strength of their army against us I fear we may be crushed."
message= _ "Then we’ll just have to make sure that no messenger escapes this valley to summon reinforcements."

events.description: Esanoo joins the elves’ effort to free the captive merfolk.

evidence.quote: message= _ "I’m fine. But I found someone who really wanted to speak with you."
message= _ "Indeed. I come from the ocean, and long have I been looking for you."
message= _ "They have been captured by the foul humans. I just barely managed to hide and escape, with the help of your friend."

message= _ "Our leader thought you might be suspicious. She said that what we must talk with you about concerns the fate of your people. Apparently it concerns ‘Yechnagoth’ and ‘Zhangor’. She said that you would understand, Kaleh."
message= _ "...It would be suicide for you to try to rescue them alone. Of course we will help you!"
message= _ "Things are coming to a head, Tanstafaal and our new friends are in trouble. Time is of the essence, so let’s move out as soon as possible."

events.description: At turn 16, captives still held are sacrificed; too few survivors means failure.
conditions: At turn 16, only captives still held are sacrificed; too few survivors causes failure.

evidence.quote: message= _ "The time has come, my brethren. On this most holy day, let us sacrifice these infidels unto The Dark Lady. Their suffering shall be a testament to her power and glory!"
message= _ "May the Sea God protect us. They are being burnt alive! It’s terrible, I can’t bear to watch."
message= _ "They are all dead. We were too late. Forgive me, wise leader!"
message= _ "We couldn’t save enough of the merfolk. We have failed. Now we shall never be able to meet the merfolk’s leader!"

events.description: Tanstafaal presents the false Eloh, who condemns Kaleh.

evidence.quote: message= _ "Wonderful! We have rescued all of my band from the humans. I cannot thank you enough."
message= _ "Curse them! The elves have freed the merfolk. We will have our vengeance. Keep fighting, and execute plan C!"
message= _ "The stinkin’ elves have freed some of the merfolk. And still they fight on. Execute plan B. And kill those merfolk!"

message= _ "I have gone on a journey and I have seen the light. No longer will I blindly follow in your footsteps, Kaleh. I have come back to lead our people on the true path. She has spoken to me, and I am but an implement of her divine will."
message= _ "Behold, our goddess has returned to us. All bow down to Eloh, our savior!"

message= _ "Yes, I speak of your so-called leader, Kaleh. I did call out to him initially because I thought he was one of the faithful, but he betrayed my trust. The humans you are slaughtering wanted to help you, until Kaleh foolishly attacked them. And now Kaleh has you serving the evil merfolk and their insidious plans. Follow his path and he would have you bow down and serve the merfolk’s foul god."
message= _ "Eloh would never ask elf to kill elf. But it seems I have little choice. My people, I have led you this far, join with me and help me crush this new rebellion!"

events.description: Zhul pleads against the fighting; the apparition immobilizes her if this scheduled scene occurs before it is defeated.
conditions: Only if the scheduled scene occurs before false Eloh is defeated.

evidence.quote: message= _ "I’m sorry Kaleh, I cannot let our people slaughter each other. There must be a way to stop this."

message= _ "Oh Eloh, you know how long I have faithfully served you. I ask you now a boon in return. Do not kill the boy Kaleh, he is just doing what his heart tells him to do. Did you not say, “To err is elven, but to forgive divine”?"

message= _ "Times have changed. Mercy is a sign of weakness. Let this be a lesson to everyone, absolute loyalty is absolute strength. It is clear that you do not understand this concept, Zhul. My people, now is a time to tear down the old guard and create a new empire of strength, fealty and glory! I shall grant those who are loyal eternal life and we will triumph over all enemies!"

message= _ "No, I don’t think you shall pester me any more. You shall be as a statue, forced to watch events unfold and helpless to interfere. Yes, I think this will be an appropriate punishment. Then perhaps you will learn not to question my divine will."

events.description: Tanstafaal kills himself after Kaleh defeats the false Eloh and offers amnesty.

evidence.quote: message= _ "Don’t worry Kaleh, we will see each other again... I promise."
message= _ "That was just an apparition, but if we meet again I will make her pay for all that she has done."
message= _ "No, do not kill him. He may deserve it, but he will not die at my hands."
message= _ "Why did he have to kill himself? Oh, poor misguided Tanstafaal. We have lost too many elves today."
message= _ "It is finished. See, my people, Tanstafaal has been killed by his own hand, and the thing pretending to be our god is gone."

message= _ "Nothing. Eloh may still watch over us, but that thing was not her. And yet, I do not hold a grudge against all of you who rebelled. I too was deceived at first, and unlike the pretender, I am merciful. For there are too few of us left for us to slaughter each other over minor grievances. Let us declare a general amnesty and unite again, going forward hand in hand, for, god or no god, I will help us find a better land, or die trying."

message= _ "I think I speak for all of us when I say that we accept your offer of amnesty and will follow you again. You have proved yourself capable as a leader and we too tire of this bloodshed. In hindsight perhaps we were wrong about Eloh and Tanstafaal; we shall have to think about this long and hard."

events.description: The merfolk propose taking four human ships so the refugees can leave.

evidence.quote: message= _ "We have picked up some knowledge of piloting while spying on the humans and we have some magical skill for controlling the winds. Once out on the open sea, our journey should be swift and safe from danger. Besides, time is pressing and our leader lives too far out in the waters to make this voyage twice."

message= _ "We have already gone to many strange places and survived. I trust the merfolk. If they believe that they can transport us safely across the waters, then I will put my life in their hands."

message= _ "There are four boats in the lagoon. Once you have captured each of the four then we can help you steer them out into the open water and to freedom. Then we can pilot them to shore, safely away from the humans, and load the rest of your people on board. But we will need all four boats to fit all of your remaining people."
message= _ "Though the cost be high, we do what we must. Come let us go capture those boats."

message= _ "Good, then let’s get out of here. The merfolk will help you guide the ships. I’ll muster the rest of our people and retreat from this bloody battlefield. We’ll meet you along the coastline west of here. Don’t worry about losing us, we’ll stick to the coast and the merfolk will help us keep in contact. Once we’ve escaped and are out of range of any counterattacks by the humans, we can load the rest of our people onto the ships."

evidence.quote: message= _ "I have captured the keep. This castle is somewhat ruined, but it will serve our purposes. Now, I wonder where the merfolk are?"

message= _ "Fear not, here we are! We have explored the southern half of the island. And except for those lizards you found, and some abandoned villages, it seem to be empty. We captured those villages for you, to help support your troops."
message= _ "Now that you have found a fortress to protect your people, we can bring in the other ships."

message= _ "Good, now we can start recruiting and recalling our warriors. Of course with so few people left, training new warriors will be very difficult and expensive. But if we lose this battle, then what use will gold be to us?"

message= _ "In our exploration we found a group of reinforcements, who were sent to help you, compliments of Melusand. You can recruit them into service at your base, if you wish. We may not be much use to you on land, but we will protect you against any threats from the water."

evidence.quote: message= _ "We’ve found both keys. Now we just have to take them and open the door to the black citadel. I tire of all this bloodshed. Wherever Yechnagoth hides, we will find her and make her pay for all she has done."
message= _ "So I see that you have finally slain both of my lieutenants. I wondered how long it would take you."

message= _ "Did you really think something as simple as a pair of keys was needed to enter and leave my sanctum? The entire thing was just a charade to see how much trouble you would go through on your pathetic little quest."

message= _ "Is that what you want? I suppose I do owe Kaleh a personal audience, after all I have put him through. Well here’s your chance. Come to me boy, and prove that you have what it takes. All you others, stay away unless you want a slow and painful death. I will deal with you later."
message= _ "I must. Too many others have died because of my actions. I couldn’t face losing you, Nym. Now it is time for me to finish it, alone."
message= _ "I’ve saved his sorry ass all this way, I’m not going to let him go and let himself get killed now!"

message= _ "Curse that girl! She’ll be the death of me. But still she doesn’t stand a chance without me. Kaleh is one thing, but Nym needs my protection. All right, I’m going in. The rest of you stand guard, if we don’t come out in half an hour then flee the island with the merfolk."

evidence.quote: message= _ "You think you killed me? You have no idea what you are facing."
